\paragraph{Layer 1 — Hopf eigenvectors (right and left).}
At $\kappa = \kappa^\star$, the right eigenvector $q$ of $J$ for the
imaginary eigenvalue $+i\omega^\star$, parametrised by $q_3 = 1$, is
%
\begin{align}
q_1 &= \frac{\gamma \left(- 2 G_{v} \kappa + 1\right)}{2 \left(G_{y} \kappa \kappa_{v} + i G_{y} \kappa \omega - i \kappa_{v} \omega + \omega^{2}\right)}, \\[4pt]
q_2 &= \frac{\gamma}{\kappa_{v} + i \omega}, \\[4pt]
q_3 &= 1.
\end{align}
%
The left eigenvector $\tilde p$ of $J^\top$ for $-i\omega^\star$, parametrised by $\tilde p_3 = 1$, is
%
\begin{align}
\tilde p_1 &= - \frac{\beta}{G_{y} \kappa + i \omega}, \\[4pt]
\tilde p_2 &= \frac{\beta \left(- 2 G_{v} \kappa + 1\right)}{2 \left(G_{y} \kappa \kappa_{v} - i G_{y} \kappa \omega + i \kappa_{v} \omega + \omega^{2}\right)}, \\[4pt]
\tilde p_3 &= 1.
\end{align}
%
Imposing the bilinear normalisation $\langle p, q\rangle := \sum_i \bar p_i\, q_i = 1$ rescales $p = \tilde p / \overline{N}$ with
%
\begin{equation}
N := \langle \tilde p, q\rangle = \frac{\beta \gamma \left(\kappa_{v} + i \omega\right) \left(2 G_{v} \kappa - 1\right) - \beta \gamma \left(2 G_{v} \kappa - 1\right) \left(G_{y} \kappa - i \omega\right) + 2 \left(\kappa_{v} + i \omega\right) \left(G_{y} \kappa - i \omega\right) \left(G_{y} \kappa \kappa_{v} + i G_{y} \kappa \omega - i \kappa_{v} \omega + \omega^{2}\right)}{2 \left(\kappa_{v} + i \omega\right) \left(G_{y} \kappa - i \omega\right) \left(G_{y} \kappa \kappa_{v} + i G_{y} \kappa \omega - i \kappa_{v} \omega + \omega^{2}\right)}.
\end{equation}
%
The accompanying gauge factor $\|q\|^2 := \sum_i \bar q_i q_i$ (which compensates for the non-unit $q$ parametrisation) is
%

Substituting $\omega^{\star 2} = c_1(\kappa^\star) = - G_{y} \kappa \left(\alpha + \kappa_{v}\right) + \alpha \kappa_{v}$ into the above eliminates $\omega^\star$ in favour of $(\kappa^\star, G_y, \kappa_v, \alpha)$.

\paragraph{Layer 3 — Closed-form $\ell_1$ (Eq.~19).}
The first Lyapunov coefficient is the gauge-corrected real part:
%
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\;
\ell_1(\kappa^\star) \;=\; \frac{1}{2\,\omega^\star \, \|q\|^2}\,
\mathrm{Re}\!\left[\, \mathcal{T}_1 + \mathcal{T}_2 + \mathcal{T}_3 \,\right]
.\;}
\tag{19}
\label{eq:ell1-closed-form-explicit}
\end{equation}
%
\paragraph{Term-power scaling and limits.} Inspection of the assembled expression yields the following structural observations:
\begin{itemize}
\item Each contraction $\mathcal{T}_k$ carries a factor of $\kappa^{\star 3}$ (one $\kappa^\star$ per non-linear vertex; $C$-vertices in $\mathcal{T}_1$ give a single $\kappa^\star$, while $\mathcal{T}_{2,3}$ contain two $B$-vertices joined by a resolvent — each $B$ contributes one $\kappa^\star$). After dividing by $2\omega^\star \|q\|^2$, the leading $\kappa^\star$-power of $\ell_1$ is $\kappa^{\star 2}$ when $\|q\|^2$ is dominated by its constant term and degenerates to $\kappa^{\star 0}$ in the opposite limit.
\item The dominant $G$-partial coefficients (by absolute monomial weight in the assembled rational) are those of $G_{aa}, G_{av}, G_{vv}$ — the second-order partials enter quadratically through both $\mathcal{T}_2$ and $\mathcal{T}_3$, whereas the third-order partials $G_{aaa}, G_{aav}, G_{avv}, G_{vvv}$ enter linearly through $\mathcal{T}_1$ only. Consequently, the sign and magnitude of $\ell_1$ near the boundary $\ell_1 = 0$ are controlled primarily by curvature ($G_{aa}, G_{vv}$) and the cross-term $G_{av}$, with the cubic terms providing a tunable shift rather than the leading mechanism.
\item \emph{Limit $\gamma \to 0$:} the leverage channel switches off, $L = \beta\gamma \to 0$, and the constant term of $H(\kappa)$ (Eq.~\ref{eq:lognorm-H}) becomes $\alpha\kappa_v(\alpha + \kappa_v) > 0$, so $H(0) > 0$ and the smallest positive root of the quadratic (when one exists) drifts to $\kappa^\star \to (\alpha + \kappa_v)/G_y$ from below; $\ell_1$ inherits this $\kappa^\star$-dependence directly. With $L = 0$, the $\beta\gamma$ term in the resolvent denominators of $\mathcal{T}_{2,3}$ vanishes, simplifying the $(2,3)$ Jacobian off-diagonal — the system decouples into a price+variance subsystem (no Hopf because the characteristic polynomial of the upper-2$\times$2 block is real-quadratic with negative product) and a memory equation that decays autonomously.
\item \emph{Limit $\alpha \to \infty$:} the memory channel becomes fast ($z$ relaxes on a vanishing timescale), $A = \alpha + \kappa_v \to \infty$, and $\kappa^\star = (G_y A^2 - G_v L - \sqrt{D})/(2 G_y^2 A) \sim A/G_y \to \infty$ — the Hopf threshold is pushed to operationally inaccessible coupling. $\ell_1$ then carries a $\kappa^{\star 2} \sim \alpha^2$ enhancement from the $\mathcal{T}_k$ vertices, but is divided by $2\omega^\star \|q\|^2$ which itself grows as $\sqrt{\alpha\kappa_v} \cdot \alpha^2$ in the leading limit; the net ratio is $\ell_1 \sim \sqrt{\alpha}$, i.e.\ supercritical Hopf becomes \emph{stronger} in the fast-memory limit.
\item \emph{Limit $\kappa_v \to \infty$ (fast variance mean-reversion):} the Heston backbone collapses to constant variance and $b(\kappa^\star) = \kappa^\star G_v - 1/2 \to -1/2$ at fixed $\kappa^\star$, so the Hopf mechanism reduces to the price$\leftrightarrow$memory feedback loop only. The closed-form $\kappa^\star$ shifts as $A^{-1} \to 0$ but the leading balance of $\ell_1$ tracks the same $\sqrt{\kappa_v}$ scaling as the $\alpha$ limit by symmetry of the formulas under $(\alpha, \kappa_v)$ swap-with-sign-conventions on $b(\kappa^\star)$.
\end{itemize}
